question: What is the primary purpose of inserting a flatus tube?

options.B: To collect stool samples for laboratory analysis
options.C: To deliver liquid nutrition directly to the colon
options.D: To relieve severe abdominal distension from trapped gas

explanation: A flatus tube creates an open channel through the anal sphincter to let trapped intestinal gas escape and relieve pressure. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T11#GNS212_U1_T11_h1)

question: When should a nurse consider using a flatus tube for a patient?

options.A: As the very first step for any mild post-operative gas pain
options.B: Before trying simple repositioning techniques in bed
options.C: After non-invasive measures like early ambulation fail to work
options.D: Whenever a patient requests relief from normal flatulence

explanation: Tubing is an invasive intervention kept for when simple actions like walking or shifting position do not clear trapped gas. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T11#GNS212_U1_T11_h1)

question: Which clinical condition is an absolute contraindication for flatus tube insertion?
explanation: Inserting a tube over fresh surgical stitches can break sutures, open wounds, and cause severe bleeding. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T11#GNS212_U1_T11_h2)

question: Why is a bleeding disorder a major risk factor for this procedure?

options.A: Coagulation defects stop the tube from passing through the sphincter
options.B: Blood thinners make the intestinal gas expand much faster
options.C: The rectal mucosa is easily traumatized and prone to hemorrhage
options.D: Clotting problems completely block the release of trapped air

explanation: The delicate lining of the rectum can easily bleed if scraped by the tube, which is dangerous for patients who cannot clot well. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T11#GNS212_U1_T11_h2)

question: What type of lubricant must be used when preparing a flatus tube?
explanation: Water-soluble lubricants are safe for mucous membranes and reduce friction without damaging rubber or plastic medical tubing. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T11#GNS212_U1_T11_h3)

question: Why is a waterproof pad placed under the patient's hips before starting?

options.A: To elevate the pelvis for easier insertion into the rectum
options.B: To protect the bed linens from accidental stool leakage
options.C: To keep the patient warm during the entire procedure
options.D: To absorb any excess water-soluble gel used on the skin

explanation: Releasing gas often expels liquid stool along with it, so a pad prevents soiling the bed and saves time on linen changes. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T11#GNS212_U1_T11_h3)

question: What is the best patient position for inserting a flatus tube?
explanation: The left lateral Sims' position matches the natural curve of the lower bowel, which eases insertion. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T11#GNS212_U1_T11_h4)

question: Why is explaining the procedure beforehand important for this task?

options.A: It prevents the patient from moving their legs during insertion
options.B: It stops the bowel from producing any more gas bubbles
options.C: It legally waives the need for a signed written consent form
options.D: It reduces anxiety and helps the patient relax their sphincter

explanation: Explaining what to expect calms the patient, reducing tension in the anal sphincter which makes the tube pass easier. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T11#GNS212_U1_T11_h4)

question: How far should a flatus tube be inserted into an adult patient?
explanation: Advancing the tube 7 to 10 centimeters ensures it safely enters the rectum past the anal sphincter without reaching the sigmoid colon. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T11#GNS212_U1_T11_h5)

question: What action must a nurse take if resistance is felt while advancing the tube?

options.A: Inject warm water to clear the blockage
options.B: Twist the tube quickly to break the barrier
options.C: Apply more pressure to push past the block
options.D: Stop immediately and do not force it

explanation: Forcing a rectal tube can cause severe trauma or perforation of the bowel wall. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T11#GNS212_U1_T11_h5)

question: What is the maximum recommended time a flatus tube should usually remain in place?
explanation: Leaving a tube in for longer periods can press against the rectal lining and cut off blood supply, leading to tissue damage. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T11#GNS212_U1_T11_h6)

question: Why is checking the abdomen after tube removal an essential nursing duty?

options.A: To confirm that abdominal distension and gas pressure have decreased
options.B: To check if the bowel sounds have completely disappeared
options.C: To ensure the anal sphincter has permanently closed shut
options.D: To measure the exact weight of the gas that escaped the body

explanation: Checking the abdomen lets the nurse evaluate if the procedure successfully met its goal of relieving trapped gas. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T11#GNS212_U1_T11_h6)

question: Which detail is essential to include in the nursing documentation for this procedure?

options.A: The exact cost of the plastic collection bag
options.B: The brand name and color of the lubricant used
options.C: Amount of gas expelled and patient tolerance
options.D: Names of all visitors present in the room

explanation: Charting must capture the clinical outcome of the procedure and how well the patient tolerated the intervention. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T11#GNS212_U1_T11_h7)

question: When should the nurse report an incident directly to the doctor during this care?

options.A: Whenever the patient falls asleep after the procedure
options.B: After every routine removal of a clean flatus tube
options.C: When normal soft stool appears on the waterproof pad
options.D: If bright red bleeding or severe pain occurs

explanation: Bleeding and severe pain are red flags indicating mucosal injury or improper insertion that needs immediate medical review. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T11#GNS212_U1_T11_h7)
